*   **Early to Mid-20th Century:**  Significant progress was made in reducing working hours through labor movements, legislation (like the Factory Acts), and union negotiations. The 40-hour work week started to become more common in the latter half of the 20th century.
*   **Late 20th Century & Early 21st Century:**  The trend continued downwards.  Average weekly hours continued to decline, though more slowly.
